 JUDGMENT 1.
The SHO, Police Station Palam Village has presented this charge-sheet against above named accused for initiation of trial U/s 279/338/323/341/34 Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short "IPC").

Prosecution Story 2. Briefly stated the case of the prosecution is that, on 21.01.2015 at about 10:45 PM, DD no.41A was recorded about a quarrel and theft of mobile phone under Palam Flyover Sector 1, Palam and another DD No. 4B was received about an injured Pawan being admitted in DDU Hospital after suffering injuries in road accident.
Based on initial information HC Subh Ram with Ct. Mahesh Kumar reached the spot where no complainant or eye witness was found.

HC Subh Ram reached DDU Hospital and received MLC no.671/15 of injured Pawan Kumar, but neither injured Pawan nor his father gave any statement and requested to police officials to take statement after they are discharged from the hospital.

On 22.01.2015, IO HC Subh Ram recorded statement of injured Pawan Kumar, who stated that on the previous evening, accused Saurabh Gupta (who was identified by his father Sanjay Kumar) driving his vehicle in high speed and in rash and negligent manner hit him wherein he sustained injuries on his ankle.

He further FIR No. 52 of 2015; P.S. Palam Village Pages 2 of 17 State v. Saurabh Gupta alleged that after the accident, some verbal abuse ensued and accused was soon joined by Jagbir Hudda and Vishal Hudda who got in physical scuffle with the injured Pawan and his father Sanjay, wherein they assaulted and pushed them both.
Based on the said complaint as well as MLC, present FIR was registered.
Investigation was undertaken where offending vehicle bearing no.DL 9S AB9539 was seized, necessary documents of the vehicle were also seized.

Offending vehicle was mechanically inspected and based on the statements as well as MLC report, chargesheet was prepared for offence punishable under Section 279/338 IPC against accused Saurabh and additionally under Section 323/341/34 IPC against all three accused persons Saurabh, Jagbir and Vishal.
Cognizance, compliance of Section 207 CrPC and Notice of accusation 3.
Based on the police report/ chargesheet filed, cognizance was taken by the Ld. Predecessor on 16.04.2015 and accused persons were summoned.
Upon appearance copy of chargesheet was supplied in compliance of Section 207 CrPC.

Notice of accusation was put to the accused Saurabh for offence punishable under Section 279/338 IPC and additionally against all three accused persons Saurabh, Jagbir and Vishal for offence punishable under Section 323/341/34 IPC on 23.03.2016,
wherein the accused persons pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.

5. Prosecution Witness (hereinafter referred to as 'PW') 1 HC Manoj, PW4 HC Dinesh and 8 Retd.
ASI Raj Pal are police officers and have formal/ limited role in the prosecution's case.
They proved the first diary entry in the police station dated 21.01.2015, receipt of offending scooty in the malkhana and receipt of original rukka dated 22.01.2015.
6. PW5 Dr. Babita, PW7 Dr. Sanjay and PW9 Dr. Ajay are Doctors appearing from DDU Hospital.

PW7 proved the MLC of injured Sanjay wherein the defence relied on the same to show that the attending doctor noted no fresh external injury even though the MLC was prepared soon after the alleged incident.
PW9 proved the MLC of injured Pawan which records referral of the patient to Orthopaedic department.

PW5 Dr. Babita is the Senior Medical Officer who confirmed the report of injured Pawan prepared by Dr. Apurva, Senior Resident, Radiology Department, DDU FIR No. 52 of 2015; P.S. Palam Village Pages 5 of 17 State v. Saurabh Gupta Hospital.
She stated that Dr. Apurva initially opined that there was no bony abnormality seen, however upon subsequent review she found 'hairline fracture of left distel shaft'.
The defence questioned PW5 wherein she answered that the report did not suggest as to who requested second opinion, or if any further x-ray or scans were conducted to reach the subsequent opinion.

PW5 further could not identify the signatures at Point X.
7.

PW2 Pawan Kumar is the injured witness and he deposed that on 21.01.2015 he alongwith his father Sanjay Kumar were returning to their home from Manglapuri Bus stop and at around 10:45 PM, they reached street no.41, Sadh Nagar, when one person (who he stated to be known to his father and he identified him in Court as Saurabh) one scooterist came from opposite side and while driving his scooter in high speed and in rash and negligent manner, hit him from the front side.
PW2 further stated that due to impact he fell down and sustained left ankle fracture and injuries on other parts of his body.
PW2 further deposed that his father picked him up and accused Saurabh who then was joined by co-accused Jagbir and Vishal, started abusing him and his father.

PW2 further alleged that quarrelling started and his father was trying to call the police, but accused persons were requesting him not to call the police and in this quarrel, they gave fist and kick blows to him as well as his father.
PW2 stated that crowd gathered at the spot and seeing this, the three accused persons fled, meanwhile his mother reached the spot and he was taken to the DDU Hospital in PCR vehicle.

PW2 further stated that in the hospital he was treated, police met him in the hospital and he chose to give his statement later, wherein the police came to his house on the next date, his complaint was written by the police and he signed the same.

PW2 identified accused Saurabh and State vs Saurabh Gupta on 15 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104747065/
4 Jagbir in Court as well as identified the scooty through photographs attached with FIR No. 52 of 2015; P.S. Palam Village Pages 6 of 17 State v. Saurabh Gupta file.
Identity of accused Vishal was not disputed.
PW2 in his cross examination admitted having known Jagbir and Vishal from before being their tenant at the previous address at RZF-100, Street no.41, Sadh Nagar,- II, Palam.
PW2 further stated that normally the place of incident is crowded but at the time of incident there was comparatively less people.
PW2 further stated that his father called the police which came in about 15-20 minutes and later stated that his mother came to the spot before the police.
PW2 further answered that neither the attending doctor asked him about the incident nor did he tell him anything.
PW2 further stated that accused Saurabh was driving the scooty alone and other two accused came after the incident from some 100 metres away.
PW2 also stated that his clothes were torn in the scuffle, but he never gave the same to the doctors or to the police.
PW2 then stated that his father was slapped by the accused persons and he was only pushed.
PW2 also stated that his father was slapped by accused Saurabh and then was slapped by other two accused Jagbir and Vishal.
PW2 denied that he was falsely implicating Jagbir and Vishal since there was some pending rent due upon them which they never paid.
8. PW3 Sanjay Kumar is the father of the injured, an eye witness to alleged accident and also himself victim in the present case.
He supported the prosecution about the date, time and place of incident as well as identified the offending vehicle as well as all three accused persons.
PW3 about assault stated that all three accused persons were abusing him and gave him fist and kick blows and his son was also beaten by the accused persons.
PW3 was first allowed to be cross examined by the Ld. APP for the State on point of arrest of all three accused persons.
PW3 denied that on 29.01.2015, he went to the police station to inquire about the progress of the case and there all three accused persons were arrested by the investigating officer in his presence.

He denied having attested the arrest of FIR No. 52 of 2015; P.S. Palam Village Pages 7 of 17 State v. Saurabh Gupta all three accused persons and even after seeing the arrest memos of all three accused persons stated that he signed the arrest memo later in the police station.

PW3 also voluntarily stated that once the SHO PS Palam Village had called him to the police station when all three accused persons were present there,
however he refused to come to police station as he already had given statement to the police.
PW3 then was cross examined by the defence wherein he admitted that there is market and shops on both sides of the road.
PW3 also admitted that cars are parked in the street no.41 and at the time of incident also cars were parked.

PW3 further admitted alleged spot was a T-point and also admitted that usually it is not possible to drive at high speed at the place of incident, however voluntarily stated that at the time of accident, accused was driving the offending vehicle at a high speed.
PW3 admitted that no number of the offending vehicle was given in the original complaint and stated that he told the vehicle number to the police at later stage.
PW3 admitted that offending vehicle is a scooty and not a scooter, however he voluntarily stated that for him both are the same.
PW3 stated that he did not know any of the person who gathered at the spot and admitted that he knew accused Jagbir since he was his tenant from 2002 to 2007.
PW3 answered that none of the people gathered at the spot tried to save him and further stated that his medical was not conducted.
He however again said that he did not remember if his medical examination was conducted.
9. PW6 ASI Subh Ram is the investigating officer in the present case who deposed about the receipt of information, reaching of the spot where they met no eye witness or injured.

PW6 further deposed State vs Saurabh Gupta on 15 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104747065/
5 about reaching DDU Hospital and receiving the MLC of injured Pawan.

He deposed about recording statement of injured Pawan and Sanjay on the next date, converting the same into tehrir which he took to police station for FIR No. 52 of 2015; P.S. Palam Village Pages 8 of 17 State v. Saurabh Gupta registration of FIR.
PW6 also deposed about arrest of accused persons, their personal search and recording of statements of PW2 as well as PW3 under Section 161 CrPC.

PW6 also deposed about serving notice under Section 133 MV Act to the owner of the offending vehicle i.e. Mr. Mahesh Kumar who replied that vehicle was being driven by his friend Saurabh Gupta at the time of alleged incident and on 29.01.2015 itself the accused brought the same to the police station.

PW6 deposed about arrest of all three accused persons, seizure of offending vehicle, driving license of accused Saurabh, seizure of registration certificate and insurance certificate of the vehicle and recording of disclosure statement of accused Saurabh and Jagbir.
PW6 was cross examined and he deposed that he did not record statement of any public/other witness except injured and his father.
PW6 further answered that he did not investigate if there existed prior tenancy between complainants and accused Jagbir and there being some dispute of recovery of rent.
PW6 denied that there was potholes at the place of incident and that vehicle cannot exceed speeds of 15 to 20 kmph.
PW6 admitted that he obtained on call details of the accused persons on the date of incident.
State of Accused under Section 313 CrPC 10.

Thereafter, on 27.04.2023 statement of accused u/S. 313 Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 were recorded wherein accused Saurabh took the plea that he did not cause any accident and was falsely implicated in the present case.
Accused Jagbir and Vishal defended of having been falsely implicated in the present case since there was some tenancy dispute with the complainant and his father.
Accused chose to lead any defense evidence.
Defence evidence FIR No. 52 of 2015; P.S. Palam Village Pages 9 of 17 State v. Saurabh Gupta 11.

Accused summoned the records of MACT 289/2016 particularly the Order dated 20.10.2015,
award dated 12.12.2020 and deposition of PW1 Pawan dated 08.12.2017 and PW2 Sanjay dated 03.04.2018 which was exhibited as Ex.DW1/A (OSR).
Final Arguments 12.
Arguments heard on behalf of State through the Ld. Additional Public Prosecutor and on behalf of accused through Ld. Counsel for accused.
Case file and evidence perused.

13. Prosecution has argued that all the ingredients of provisions have been established as deposed by the nine witnesses and there is nothing to suggest the contrary and therefore, it is averred that prosecution has proved the case beyond reasonable doubt.
The defence on the other hand has argued that PW2 and PW3 have been inconsistent in their testimonies about the scuffle as well as assault.

Defence argued that the medical documents were never proved since the doctor who prepared the X-ray report was never examined and none from the orthopaedic or radiology department was examined to explain the two different opinions expressed on the same x-ray report.

Defense also relied on the testimonies of Pawan Kumar and Sanjay Kumar given in MACT no.

6 289/2016 where they denied any scuffle or quarrel having taken place at the place of incident after the accident.

sentences.text: Even the identity of the offending vehicle has been argued to have been not established beyond reasonable doubts.
Appraisal of evidence 14.

After hearing ld. APP for the state and ld. counsel for the accused and having gone through the case file carefully and meticulously, this court is of the opinion that qua allegations of road accident,
the following points FIR No. 52 of 2015; P.S. Palam Village Pages 10 of 17 State v. Saurabh Gupta for determination arise, firstly, whether the offending vehicle was involved in the accident in question;
secondly, whether the accused Saurabh was driving the vehicle at the time of incident; and thirdly whether on accused drove the offending vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and thereby caused grievous hurt to Pawan.
15.

Further, qua quarrel which allegedly ensured after the accident, the point of determination is whether all three accused persons Saurabh, Jagbir and Vishal in furtherance of their common intention wrongfully restrained and assaulted the complainant Pawan and his father Sanjay.
16. Before proceeding to the merits, it is admitted fact in the present case that both injured Pawan and Sanjay are known to Jagbir and Vishal.
Pawan is son of Sanjay and they were tenant of Jagbir from 2002 to 2008, whose son is Vishal.
Defence has heavily relied on this prior tenancy relationship to argue that there was dispute as to non-payment of rent and therefore they have been falsely implicated in the present case.
Another admitted fact is MACT 289/2016 filed by the complainant against accused Saurabh.

In the said proceedings, complainant was awarded Rupees one and half lacs as compensation and there during deposition both Pawan (PW1 therein) and Sanjay (PW2 therein) stated that no quarrel took place after the alleged incident.
Sanjay (as PW2 in MACT 289/2016) during cross examination dated 03.04.2018 even admitted that he cannot tell the model and color of the scooty involved in the accident.
Pawan (as PW1 in MACT 289/2016) during his cross examination dated 08.12.2017 guessed that color of the scooty was white and its make was Honda Activa.

17. Coming to the records of the present case, PW2 Pawan (in his deposition dated 22.01.2018)
identified the offending vehicle from photographs Ex.P1 FIR No. 52 of 2015; P.S. Palam Village Pages 11 of 17 State v. Saurabh Gupta which shows one scooty bearing no. DL 9S AB9539 make Honda Aviator and color is Pearl Black.
Further, the original tehrir makes no mention of the vehicle number as is missing even from the FIR.
The site plan Ex.PW3/A allegedly prepared at the instance of PW3 Sanjay Kumar is doubtful.
The said site plan at the bottom portion make a 'note' written in Hindi language, however the signatures of witness Sanjay Kumar appears to have been taken before the said 'note'.
It can clearly be seen in site plan Ex.PW3/A that the indent of the 'note' is not in one single indentation, font or line spacing.
The 'note' which starts with much more space and bigger font at the beginning three lines, can been seen to have lesser line spacing for the bottom four lines and even the font size is reduced.

The last two lines of the said note have been written to accommodate the signatures of PW3 Sanjay which clearly shows that the signature of PW3 Sanjay was taken before and later the 'note' in Hindi was written.

Even the difference in font size and line State vs Saurabh Gupta on 15 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104747065/
7 spacing is done to accommodate the signatures of IO/HC Shub Ram at the bottom.
Said fact is utmost relevant as this site plan for the first time mentions the vehicle number is mentioned in the present case.
18. Further, the first diary entry DD No. 41A was about one quarrel and snatching of mobile phones.

The said information does not mention the names of the caller or of the assailant, even though PW3 admits to have known all three accused persons since before and even PW2 knew the accused Jagbir and Vishal from before.

Further, when the police met the two injured persons in the hospital, both refused to give their statement, even though none were admitted for long or were not declared unfit for statement by the doctors.
FIR No. 52 of 2015; P.S. Palam Village Pages 12 of 17 State v. Saurabh Gupta 19.
PW2 never gave the registration number of vehicle in his entire police complaint or statement under Section 161 CrPC.
PW3 also never gave the number of vehicle before police and it is only in the site plan that the vehicle number has been mentioned.
PW3 during cross examination in the Court even stated that when he reached police station, the IO had already seized the offending vehicle.
It is incomprehensible as to how the investigating officer came to know about the offending vehicle when neither Pawan nor Sanjay mentioned the registration number before police.
The offending vehicle in the present case was first recovered and then same was shown to Sanjay.
The incident is of 2015, until the year 2017 and 2018 both Sanjay and Pawan could not identify the offending vehicle before the MACT Court in 289/2016.
Further, Pawan did mention the make of offending vehicle as Honda Activa of white color, whereas before this Court the offending vehicle is of Pearl Black color of make Honda Aviator.
20. There appears genuine dispute as to identity of the offending vehicle from the discrepancies pointed out above.
Both Pawan and Sanjay have not acted naturally and never made any disclosure about identity of offending vehicle and investigating officer on his own seized the vehicle.
Since the prosecution has miserably failed to establish the identity of the offending vehicle, the first set of charge is not established against accused Saurabh.

Since offending vehicle being involved in present alleged accident has not been proved beyond reasonable doubt, there is no need for further discussion that accused Saurabh was driving the offending vehicle and the same was in rash and negligent manner.
21. Even for the sake of wastage of ink, both PW2 Pawan and PW3 Sanjay merely stated opinion of fact that alleged offending vehicle was being driven in rash and negligent manner at high speed.

Neither any fact was FIR No. 52 of 2015; P.S. Palam Village Pages 13 of 17 State v. Saurabh Gupta stated as to the actual speed of the vehicle and the actual manner of driving which can be termed as rash and negligent.
PW2 and PW3 are witness of fact and not opinion, their mere statement that vehicle was being driven in rash and negligent manner can be statement of opinion and not fact.
They both being witness of fact ought to have clearly stated that manner in which the offending vehicle was being driven and manner in which it came and hit the victim.

State vs Saurabh Gupta on 15 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104747065/
8 22.
The above deposition is noteworthy only for the purpose of discrediting the two witnesses PW2 and PW3.
As already highlighted PW2 and PW3 have changed their stands qua identifying the offending vehicle.
PW2 and PW3 have complete opposite testimonies as to identity of offending vehicle before the MACT claim no. 289/16, South West and before this Court.
Not even the make and color of the vehicle is same in their depositions.

There is a difference of night and day in the statement of injured Pawan wherein within two months he stated that color of vehicle to be white before MACT (on 08.12.2017) and identified one Pearl Black color scooty before this Court as the offending vehicle (on 22.01.2018).
23. Both PW2 Pawan and PW3 Sanjay have been inconsistent in their individual testimonies and when read together, they have discredited each other.

PW2 stated that there was verbal dispute and scuffle wherein his father was first slapped by accused Saurabh and then by accused Jagbir and Vishal, whereas he alleged to have only been pushed by the accused persons.
PW3 however, stated that he was given fist and kick blows by the accused persons and his son was also assaulted and beaten by the accused persons.
The MLC of PW2 and PW3 does not at all support the said allegations.
PW3 was found to have no external injuries visible during his MLC, not even a scratch has been mentioned.

PW2 also apart from having FIR No. 52 of 2015; P.S. Palam Village Pages 14 of 17 State v. Saurabh Gupta pain in his elbow and having been referred to orthopaedic department has not been mentioned to have sustained any injuries.
Even their MLC does not mention having been assaulted by three named accused persons and victim Pawan having sustained injuries due to accident by any scooty.
24. Another missing crucial piece of evidence is absence of public witness.
Investigating Officer made no effort to trace any eye witness or first responder to the incident.

It is true that the time of incident is 10:45 PM and there is possibility that incident was witnessed by a small number of people, however the complainant and victim stated that the place of incident has residential houses as well as shops, which means there were local and permanent residents available nearby and someone of the locality could have deposed in support of the victims and prosecution.

Further, the incident is of the year 2015 and it is hard to believe that there would not be available any CCTV footage at or near the place of incident, especially when the locality is residential and has many shops.
Atleast, some footage could have been made available to corroborate the actual event or facts or circumstances which occurred before or after the alleged incident.
25. There is no conclusive proof that complainant sustained injuries due to accident caused by offending vehicle.
Same is also supported by mechanical inspection report Ex.A1 which found only one brushing over front leg guard and mudguard and also some brushing at silencer.
The same cannot be linked to the alleged hit sustained by the victim Pawan from the front.
This is over and above the fact that prosecution has failed to prove that it was this vehicle bearing no. DL 9S AB9539 which was involved in the alleged accident.
FIR No. 52 of 2015; P.S. Palam Village Pages 15 of 17 State v. Saurabh Gupta State vs Saurabh Gupta on 15 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104747065/

sentences.text: From the said finding, it is quite improbable to impute any rash and negligent driving on the accused.
Firstly, there is no proof beyond reasonable doubt that the offending vehicle is the same which was involved in the accident.
There is also no conclusive proof that victim got hit by the offending vehicle since the inspection report records no such damage to the offending vehicle.
Moreover, there is no proof of rash and negligent act of the driver of the vehicle.
A mere textbook statement of injured that vehicle was being driven in rash and negligent manner is a statement of opinion and not of fact.
An injured victim ought to depose the manner in which the vehicle was being driven for the Court of law to interpret the mens rea, whether same was reckless and amounts to rash and negligent driving.

Besides, the prosecution never could prove the two different medical opinion based on same x-ray report and further it could not be established that any injury at the left ankle of PW2 Pawan Kumar was sustained as a result of accident by scooty.
27. Be that as it may, nothing precluded the State from tracing eye witnesses, search CCTV footage or even conduct test identification parade of the accused.
The site plan Ex.PW3/A has manipulation after it was signed by PW3 Sanjay and IO.
The note in Hindi language can clearly be seen to have been written at a subsequent time wherein for the first time the number of vehicle has been mentioned.
28. It is trite in criminal jurisprudence that the prosecution is under an obligation to prove its case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt.
The standard of proof to be adopted in criminal cases is not merely of preponderance of probabilities but proof beyond reasonable doubt on the basis of cogent, convincing and reliable evidence.
It is also well settled that in case of doubt, the benefit must necessarily be allowed to the accused.
FIR No. 52 of 2015; P.S. Palam Village Pages 16 of 17 State v. Saurabh Gupta Findings 29

. The prosecution thus has thus failed to prove beyond reasonable doubt that accused Saurabh was driving the offending vehicle DL 9S AB9539 and while driving the same, in rash and negligent manner so as to endanger life and personal safety of humans and caused accident causing grievous injury to victim Pawan.
Further, the medical documents of both Pawan and Sanjay does not support their allegations of beatings and blows by kicks and fists.
Thus none of the charges are proved to have been established beyond reasonable doubts.
FINAL ORDER 30.

In view of the above reasons accused Saurabh Gupta is acquitted for offence punishable u/S.
279/338 IPC; further accused persons Saurabh Gupta, Jagbir Hudda and Vishal Hudda are acquitted for offence punishable u/S. 323/341/34 IPC.

opennyai_summary.arguments:
13. Prosecution has argued that all the ingredients of provisions have been established as deposed by the nine witnesses and there is nothing to suggest the contrary and therefore, it is averred that prosecution has proved the case beyond reasonable doubt.
The defence on the other hand has argued that PW2 and PW3 have been inconsistent in their testimonies about the scuffle as well as assault.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
FIR No. 52 of 2015; P.S. Palam Village Pages 12 of 17 State v. Saurabh Gupta 19.
PW2 never gave the registration number of vehicle in his entire police complaint or statement under Section 161 CrPC.
Both Pawan and Sanjay have not acted naturally and never made any disclosure about identity of offending vehicle and investigating officer on his own seized the vehicle.
Since the prosecution has miserably failed to establish the identity of the offending vehicle, the first set of charge is not established against accused Saurabh.
Since offending vehicle being involved in present alleged accident has not been proved beyond reasonable doubt, there is no need for further discussion that accused Saurabh was driving the offending vehicle and the same was in rash and negligent manner.
21. Even for the sake of wastage of ink, both PW2 Pawan and PW3 Sanjay merely stated opinion of fact that alleged offending vehicle was being driven in rash and negligent manner at high speed.
Neither any fact was FIR No. 52 of 2015; P.S. Palam Village Pages 13 of 17 State v. Saurabh Gupta stated as to the actual speed of the vehicle and the actual manner of driving which can be termed as rash and negligent.
PW2 and PW3 are witness of fact and not opinion, their mere statement that vehicle was being driven in rash and negligent manner can be statement of opinion and not fact.
They both being witness of fact ought to have clearly stated that manner in which the offending vehicle was being driven and manner in which it came and hit the victim.
The same cannot be linked to the alleged hit sustained by the victim Pawan from the front.
This is over and above the fact that prosecution has failed to prove that it was this vehicle bearing no. DL 9S AB9539 which was involved in the alleged accident.
FIR No. 52 of 2015; P.S. Palam Village Pages 15 of 17 State v. Saurabh Gupta State vs Saurabh Gupta on 15 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104747065/
From the said finding, it is quite improbable to impute any rash and negligent driving on the accused.
Firstly, there is no proof beyond reasonable doubt that the offending vehicle is the same which was involved in the accident.
There is also no conclusive proof that victim got hit by the offending vehicle since the inspection report records no such damage to the offending vehicle.
Moreover, there is no proof of rash and negligent act of the driver of the vehicle.
A mere textbook statement of injured that vehicle was being driven in rash and negligent manner is a statement of opinion and not of fact.
An injured victim ought to depose the manner in which the vehicle was being driven for the Court of law to interpret the mens rea, whether same was reckless and amounts to rash and negligent driving.
Besides, the prosecution never could prove the two different medical opinion based on same x-ray report and further it could not be established that any injury at the left ankle of PW2 Pawan Kumar was sustained as a result of accident by scooty.
27. Be that as it may, nothing precluded the State from tracing eye witnesses, search CCTV footage or even conduct test identification parade of the accused.
The note in Hindi language can clearly be seen to have been written at a subsequent time wherein for the first time the number of vehicle has been mentioned.
28. It is trite in criminal jurisprudence that the prosecution is under an obligation to prove its case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt.
The standard of proof to be adopted in criminal cases is not merely of preponderance of probabilities but proof beyond reasonable doubt on the basis of cogent, convincing and reliable evidence.
It is also well settled that in case of doubt, the benefit must necessarily be allowed to the accused.
. The prosecution thus has thus failed to prove beyond reasonable doubt that accused Saurabh was driving the offending vehicle DL 9S AB9539 and while driving the same, in rash and negligent manner so as to endanger life and personal safety of humans and caused accident causing grievous injury to victim Pawan.
Further, the medical documents of both Pawan and Sanjay does not support their allegations of beatings and blows by kicks and fists.
Thus none of the charges are proved to have been established beyond reasonable doubts.
